latin: Quis potis est dignum pollenti pectore carmen
en: Who has the strength of heart to build a song worthy

latin: condere pro rerum maiestate hisque repertis?
en: of the majesty of things and of these discoveries?

latin: quisve valet verbis tantum, qui fingere laudes
en: Or who is so strong in words that he could shape praises

latin: pro meritis eius possit, qui talia nobis
en: to match the merits of the one who left us such prizes,

latin: pectore parta suo quaesitaque praemia liquit?
en: brought forth and sought out by his own heart?

latin: nemo, ut opinor, erit mortali corpore cretus.
en: No one, I think, who is made of a mortal body.

latin: nam si, ut ipsa petit maiestas cognita rerum,
en: For if we must speak as the known majesty of things

latin: dicendum est, deus ille fuit, deus, inclyte Memmi,
en: itself demands, he was a god, a god, renowned Memmius,

latin: qui princeps vitae rationem invenit eam quae
en: who first discovered that reasoning of life which

latin: nunc appellatur sapientia, quique per artem
en: is now called wisdom, and who by his art

latin: fluctibus et tantis vitam tantisque tenebris
en: took life out of such great waves and such great darkness

latin: in tam tranquillo et tam clara luce locavit.
en: and set it in so calm a place and in so clear a light.

latin: confer enim divina aliorum antiqua reperta.
en: For compare the godlike discoveries of others long ago.

latin: namque Ceres fertur fruges Liberque liquoris
en: For Ceres is said to have established grain, and Liber

latin: vitigeni laticem mortalibus instituisse;
en: for mortals the liquid of the vine-born juice;

latin: cum tamen his posset sine rebus vita manere,
en: and yet life could go on without these things,

latin: ut fama est aliquas etiam nunc vivere gentis.
en: as report says some nations live even now.

latin: at bene non poterat sine puro pectore vivi;
en: But a good life was not possible without a pure heart;

latin: quo magis hic merito nobis deus esse videtur,
en: so with all the more right this man seems to us a god,

latin: ex quo nunc etiam per magnas didita gentis
en: from whom even now, spread abroad through great nations,

latin: dulcia permulcent animos solacia vitae.
en: the sweet consolations of life soothe our minds.

latin: Herculis antistare autem si facta putabis,
en: But if you think the deeds of Hercules stand above his,

latin: longius a vera multo ratione ferere.
en: you will be carried much farther from true reasoning.

latin: quid Nemeaeus enim nobis nunc magnus hiatus
en: For what harm to us now would that great gaping mouth

latin: ille leonis obesset et horrens Arcadius sus,
en: of the Nemean lion do, or the bristling Arcadian boar?

latin: tanto opere officerent nobis Stymphala colentes?
en: And how much could they hinder us, the birds that haunt Stymphalus?

latin: denique quid Cretae taurus Lernaeaque pestis
en: Finally, what could the bull of Crete do, or the plague of Lerna,

latin: hydra venenatis posset vallata colubris?
en: the hydra, palisaded round with venomous snakes?

latin: quidve tripectora tergemini vis Geryonai
en: Or what the triple-breasted strength of three-bodied Geryon,

latin: et Diomedis equi spirantes naribus ignem
en: and the horses of Diomedes, breathing fire from their nostrils

latin: Thracia Bistoniasque plagas atque Ismara propter
en: in Thrace, near the Bistonian lands and Ismarus,

latin: aureaque Hesperidum servans fulgentia mala,
en: and, guarding the gleaming golden apples of the Hesperides,

latin: asper, acerba tuens, immani corpore serpens
en: fierce, with savage glare, the serpent of enormous body

latin: arboris amplexus stirpes? quid denique obesset
en: coiled round the tree's trunk? What harm, finally, would it do

latin: propter Atlanteum litus pelagique severa,
en: there by the Atlantic shore and the stern stretches of the sea,

latin: quo neque noster adit quisquam nec barbarus audet?
en: where no one of ours goes and no barbarian dares?

latin: cetera de genere hoc quae sunt portenta perempta,
en: And the other monsters of this kind that have been destroyed,

latin: si non victa forent, quid tandem viva nocerent?
en: if they had not been conquered, what harm, pray, would they do alive?

latin: nil, ut opinor: ita ad satiatem terra ferarum
en: None, I think: for even now the earth swarms, to the full,

latin: nunc etiam scatit et trepido terrore repleta est
en: with wild beasts, and is filled with trembling terror

latin: per nemora ac montes magnos silvasque profundas;
en: through groves and great mountains and deep forests,

latin: quae loca vitandi plerumque est nostra potestas.
en: places which for the most part it is in our power to avoid.

latin: at nisi purgatumst pectus, quae proelia nobis
en: But unless the heart is purged, what battles then

latin: atque pericula tumst ingratis insinuandum!
en: and dangers must work their way into us against our will!

latin: quantae tum scindunt hominem cuppedinis acres
en: How great then are the sharp cares of desire that tear

latin: sollicitum curae quantique perinde timores!
en: a troubled man apart, and how great, too, the fears!

latin: quidve superbia spurcitia ac petulantia? quantas
en: Or pride, filth, and wantonness, what of them? How great

latin: efficiunt clades! quid luxus desidiaeque?
en: the disasters they bring about! What of luxury and sloth?

latin: haec igitur qui cuncta subegerit ex animoque
en: Therefore the man who has subdued all these and from the mind

latin: expulerit dictis, non armis, nonne decebit
en: driven them out with words, not arms, will it not be fitting

latin: hunc hominem numero divom dignarier esse?
en: that this man be deemed worthy of a place among the gods?

latin: cum bene praesertim multa ac divinitus ipsis
en: Especially since he was wont to give, well and divinely,

latin: iam mortalibus e divis dare dicta suerit
en: many sayings from the gods to mortals themselves

latin: atque omnem rerum naturam pandere dictis.
en: and to lay open in his words the whole nature of things.

latin: Cuius ego ingressus vestigia dum rationes
en: Treading in his footsteps, while I follow out his reasonings

latin: persequor ac doceo dictis, quo quaeque creata
en: and teach in my words by what covenant all things

latin: foedere sint, in eo quam sit durare necessum
en: are created, and how they must endure in it,

latin: nec validas valeant aevi rescindere leges,
en: and cannot annul the strong laws of time,

latin: quo genere in primis animi natura reperta est
en: in which kind, first of all, the nature of the mind was found

latin: nativo primum consistere corpore creta,
en: to consist, first, of a body that had birth,

latin: nec posse incolumem magnum durare per aevum,
en: and not able to endure unharmed through long ages,

latin: sed simulacra solere in somnis fallere mentem,
en: but that images are wont to deceive the mind in sleep

latin: cernere cum videamur eum quem vita reliquit,
en: when we seem to see one whom life has left;

latin: quod super est, nunc huc rationis detulit ordo,
en: for the rest, the order of reasoning has now brought me to this,

latin: ut mihi mortali consistere corpore mundum
en: that I must give an account of how the world consists

latin: nativomque simul ratio reddunda sit esse;
en: of a mortal body and at the same time had a birth;

latin: et quibus ille modis congressus materiai
en: and in what ways that coming-together of matter

latin: fundarit terram caelum mare sidera solem
en: founded the earth, the sky, the sea, the stars, the sun,

latin: lunaique globum; tum quae tellure animantes
en: and the globe of the moon; then what living things

latin: extiterint, et quae nullo sint tempore natae;
en: arose from the earth, and which were at no time born;

latin: quove modo genus humanum variante loquella
en: and in what way the human race, with varied speech,

latin: coeperit inter se vesci per nomina rerum;
en: began to make use, among themselves, of the names of things;

latin: et quibus ille modis divom metus insinuarit
en: and in what ways that fear of the gods worked its way into

latin: pectora, terrarum qui in orbi sancta tuetur
en: our hearts, that fear which over the round of the earth keeps holy

latin: fana lacus lucos aras simulacraque divom.
en: shrines, lakes, groves, altars, and images of the gods.

latin: praeterea solis cursus lunaeque meatus
en: Further, the courses of the sun and the wanderings of the moon,

latin: expediam qua vi flectat natura gubernans;
en: I shall explain by what force steering nature bends them,

latin: ne forte haec inter caelum terramque reamur
en: so that we may not think these, between heaven and earth,

latin: libera sponte sua cursus lustrare perennis,
en: run their everlasting courses freely, of their own accord,

latin: morigera ad fruges augendas atque animantis,
en: obliging the growth of crops and of living things,

latin: neve aliqua divom volvi ratione putemus.
en: nor suppose they are rolled round by some reasoning of the gods.

latin: nam bene qui didicere deos securum agere aevom,
en: For those who have learned well that the gods lead a life without care,

latin: si tamen interea mirantur qua ratione
en: if yet meanwhile they wonder by what principle

latin: quaeque geri possint, praesertim rebus in illis
en: each thing can be carried on, above all in those things

latin: quae supera caput aetheriis cernuntur in oris,
en: that are seen overhead in the shores of the ether,

latin: rursus in antiquas referuntur religiones
en: are carried back again into the old religions

latin: et dominos acris adsciscunt, omnia posse
en: and take on harsh masters, whom the wretches believe

latin: quos miseri credunt, ignari quid queat esse,
en: can do all things, ignorant of what can come to be

latin: quid nequeat, finita potestas denique cuique
en: and what cannot, and how at last each thing's power is bounded,

latin: qua nam sit ratione atque alte terminus haerens.
en: by what principle, and its boundary-stone set deep.

latin: Quod super est, ne te in promissis plura moremur,
en: For the rest, not to keep you longer with promises,

latin: principio maria ac terras caelumque tuere;
en: first of all look on the seas and lands and sky;

latin: quorum naturam triplicem, tria corpora, Memmi,
en: their threefold nature, their three bodies, Memmius,

latin: tris species tam dissimilis, tria talia texta,
en: three appearances so unlike, three such weavings,

latin: una dies dabit exitio, multosque per annos
en: one day will give to destruction, and, upheld through many years,

latin: sustentata ruet moles et machina mundi.
en: the mass and machinery of the world will fall.

latin: nec me animi fallit quam res nova miraque menti
en: Nor does it escape my mind how new and strange a thing

latin: accidat exitium caeli terraeque futurum,
en: befalls the mind, the coming destruction of heaven and earth,

latin: et quam difficile id mihi sit pervincere dictis;
en: and how hard it is for me to prove it in words;

latin: ut fit ubi insolitam rem adportes auribus ante
en: as happens when you bring to the ears a thing unheard of before

latin: nec tamen hanc possis oculorum subdere visu
en: yet cannot put it under the sight of the eyes

latin: nec iacere indu manus, via qua munita fidei
en: nor lay it in the hands, by which the paved road of belief

latin: proxima fert humanum in pectus templaque mentis.
en: leads nearest to the human heart and the precincts of the mind.

latin: sed tamen effabor. dictis dabit ipsa fidem res
en: But still I will speak out. Perhaps the fact itself will give belief

latin: forsitan et graviter terrarum motibus ortis
en: to my words, and you will see, when violent earthquakes arise,

latin: omnia conquassari in parvo tempore cernes.
en: all things shaken to pieces in a little time.

latin: quod procul a nobis flectat fortuna gubernans,
en: May steering fortune turn this far away from us,

latin: et ratio potius quam res persuadeat ipsa
en: and may reasoning rather than the event itself persuade

latin: succidere horrisono posse omnia victa fragore.
en: that all things can be overcome and fall with a dreadful crash.

latin: Qua prius adgrediar quam de re fundere fata
en: Before I approach this subject, to pour out pronouncements

latin: sanctius et multo certa ratione magis quam
en: more holy and with far surer reasoning than

latin: Pythia quae tripode a Phoebi lauroque profatur,
en: the Pythia, who speaks from the tripod and the laurel of Phoebus,

latin: multa tibi expediam doctis solacia dictis;
en: I shall set out for you many consolations in learned words,

latin: religione refrenatus ne forte rearis
en: so that, reined in by religion, you may not think

latin: terras et solem et caelum, mare sidera lunam,
en: that the lands and sun and sky, sea, stars, moon,

latin: corpore divino debere aeterna manere,
en: must remain eternal, being of divine body,

latin: proptereaque putes ritu par esse Gigantum
en: and so suppose it right that, like the Giants,

latin: pendere eos poenas inmani pro scelere omnis,
en: all those should pay the penalty for monstrous crime

latin: qui ratione sua disturbent moenia mundi
en: who by their reasoning shake the walls of the world

latin: praeclarumque velint caeli restinguere solem
en: and would put out the glorious sun of heaven,

latin: inmortalia mortali sermone notantes;
en: branding immortal things with mortal speech;

latin: quae procul usque adeo divino a numine distent
en: although these are so very far removed from divine power

latin: inque deum numero quae sint indigna videri,
en: and so unworthy to be counted among the gods

latin: notitiam potius praebere ut posse putentur
en: that they may rather be thought to give us a notion

latin: quid sit vitali motu sensuque remotum.
en: of what is removed from vital motion and sense.

latin: quippe etenim non est, cum quovis corpore ut esse
en: For indeed it cannot be that with any body whatever

latin: posse animi natura putetur consiliumque.
en: the nature of the mind and judgment be thought able to exist.

latin: sicut in aethere non arbor, non aequore salso
en: Just as there can be no tree in the upper air, no clouds

latin: nubes esse queunt neque pisces vivere in arvis
en: in the salt sea, nor can fish live in the fields,

latin: nec cruor in lignis neque saxis sucus inesse,
en: nor blood be in wood, nor sap in stones;

latin: certum ac dispositumst ubi quicquid crescat et insit,
en: it is fixed and ordered where each thing grows and is:

latin: sic animi natura nequit sine corpore oriri
en: so the nature of the mind cannot arise without the body,

latin: sola neque a nervis et sanguine longius esse.
en: alone, nor exist far off from sinews and blood.

latin: quod si posset enim, multo prius ipsa animi vis
en: For if it could, the force of the mind itself, much sooner,

latin: in capite aut umeris aut imis calcibus esse
en: could be in the head or shoulders or the lowest heels,

latin: posset et innasci quavis in parte soleret,
en: and would be wont to be born in any part you please,

latin: tandem in eodem homine atque in eodem vase manere.
en: and still remain in the same man and the same vessel.

latin: quod quoniam nostro quoque constat corpore certum
en: And since even in our body it is evidently fixed

latin: dispositumque videtur ubi esse et crescere possit
en: and ordered, it seems, where each can be and grow,

latin: seorsum anima atque animus, tanto magis infitiandum
en: spirit and mind, each apart, all the more must we deny

latin: totum posse extra corpus formamque animalem
en: that, wholly outside the body and the living form,

latin: putribus in glebis terrarum aut solis in igni
en: they could endure in crumbling clods of earth or the sun's fire

latin: aut in aqua durare aut altis aetheris oris.
en: or in water or the high shores of the ether.

latin: haud igitur constant divino praedita sensu,
en: Therefore these things do not exist endowed with divine sense,

latin: quandoquidem nequeunt vitaliter esse animata.
en: since they cannot be alive and quickened with the breath of life.

latin: Illud item non est ut possis credere, sedes
en: Again, you cannot possibly believe that the holy

latin: esse deum sanctas in mundi partibus ullis.
en: dwellings of the gods exist in any parts of the world.

latin: tenvis enim natura deum longeque remota
en: For the nature of the gods is thin, and far removed

latin: sensibus ab nostris animi vix mente videtur;
en: from our senses, and is scarcely seen by the thought of the mind;

latin: quae quoniam manuum tactum suffugit et ictum,
en: and since it slips away from the touch and stroke of hands,

latin: tactile nil nobis quod sit contingere debet;
en: it must touch nothing that is tangible to us;

latin: tangere enim non quit quod tangi non licet ipsum.
en: for what may not itself be touched cannot touch.

latin: quare etiam sedes quoque nostris sedibus esse
en: Therefore their dwellings too must also be unlike

latin: dissimiles debent, tenues de corpore eorum;
en: our dwellings, thin, in keeping with their bodies;

latin: quae tibi posterius largo sermone probabo.
en: and this I shall prove to you later in ample discourse.

latin: Dicere porro hominum causa voluisse parare
en: Further, to say that for the sake of men they willed to prepare

latin: praeclaram mundi naturam proptereaque
en: the glorious nature of the world, and that therefore

latin: adlaudabile opus divom laudare decere
en: it is fitting to praise the praiseworthy work of the gods,

latin: aeternumque putare atque inmortale futurum,
en: and to think that it will be eternal and immortal,

latin: nec fas esse, deum quod sit ratione vetusta
en: and that it is sin that what, by the gods' ancient reasoning,

latin: gentibus humanis fundatum perpetuo aevo,
en: was founded for the races of men to last through endless age,

latin: sollicitare suis ulla vi ex sedibus umquam
en: should ever be shaken by any force from its seat,

latin: nec verbis vexare et ab imo evertere summa,
en: or harried with words and overturned from top to bottom,

latin: cetera de genere hoc adfingere et addere, Memmi,
en: and to invent and add other things of this kind, Memmius,

latin: desiperest. quid enim inmortalibus atque beatis
en: is folly. For what profit could our gratitude

latin: gratia nostra queat largirier emolumenti,
en: bestow upon immortal and blessed beings,

latin: ut nostra quicquam causa gerere adgrediantur?
en: that for our sake they should set about doing anything?

latin: quidve novi potuit tanto post ante quietos
en: Or what new thing could, so long after, lure beings at peace before

latin: inlicere ut cuperent vitam mutare priorem?
en: to desire to change their former life?

latin: nam gaudere novis rebus debere videtur
en: For it seems that one should rejoice in new things

latin: cui veteres obsunt; sed cui nihil accidit aegri
en: whom the old things harm; but one who met with nothing grievous

latin: tempore in ante acto, cum pulchre degeret aevom,
en: in the time gone by, while he spent his life in beauty,

latin: quid potuit novitatis amorem accendere tali?
en: what could kindle in such a one a love of novelty?

latin: quidve mali fuerat nobis non esse creatis?
en: Or what harm would it have been to us never to have been created?

latin: an, credo, in tenebris vita ac maerore iacebat,
en: Did life, I suppose, lie in darkness and sorrow

latin: donec diluxit rerum genitalis origo?
en: until the generative origin of things dawned?

latin: natus enim debet qui cumque est velle manere
en: For whoever has been born must want to remain

latin: in vita, donec retinebit blanda voluptas;
en: in life, so long as soft pleasure holds him;

latin: qui numquam vero vitae gustavit amorem
en: but for one who never tasted the love of life

latin: nec fuit in numero, quid obest non esse creatum?
en: and was never counted, what harm is it not to have been created?

latin: exemplum porro gignundis rebus et ipsa
en: Further, the pattern for creating things, and the very

latin: notities hominum divis unde insita primum est,
en: notion of men, from where was it first planted in the gods,

latin: quid vellent facere ut scirent animoque viderent,
en: so that they knew and saw in their mind what they wished to make,

latin: quove modost umquam vis cognita principiorum
en: or in what way was the power of the beginnings ever known,

latin: quidque inter sese permutato ordine possent.
en: and what they could do with their order changed among themselves,

latin: si non ipsa dedit speciem natura creandi?
en: if nature herself did not give a likeness of creation?

latin: namque ita multa modis multis primordia rerum
en: For so many first-beginnings of things, in so many ways,

latin: ex infinito iam tempore percita plagis
en: driven by blows from infinite time till now,

latin: ponderibusque suis consuerunt concita ferri
en: and roused by their own weights, have been used to move

latin: omnimodisque coire atque omnia pertemptare,
en: and to meet in every way and to try out all things

latin: quae cumque inter se possint congressa creare,
en: that they could create by meeting with one another,

latin: ut non sit mirum, si in talis disposituras
en: so it is no wonder if they fell into such arrangements

latin: deciderunt quoque et in talis venere meatus,
en: and have come, as well, into such courses

latin: qualibus haec rerum geritur nunc summa novando.
en: as those by which this sum of things is now carried on by renewal.

latin: Quod si iam rerum ignorem primordia quae sint,
en: But even if I did not know what the first-beginnings of things are,

latin: hoc tamen ex ipsis caeli rationibus ausim
en: this, still, from the very order of heaven I would dare

latin: confirmare aliisque ex rebus reddere multis,
en: to affirm, and to show from many other things,

latin: nequaquam nobis divinitus esse paratam
en: that by no means for us, by divine power, was prepared

latin: naturam rerum: tanta stat praedita culpa.
en: the nature of things: so great the flaws it stands endowed with.

latin: principio quantum caeli tegit impetus ingens,
en: First, of all that the vast sweep of heaven covers,

latin: inde avidam partem montes silvaeque ferarum
en: a greedy portion the mountains and the forests of wild beasts

latin: possedere, tenent rupes vastaeque paludes
en: have taken; rocks hold it, and vast marshes,

latin: et mare, quod late terrarum distinet oras.
en: and the sea, which keeps the shores of the lands wide apart.

latin: inde duas porro prope partis fervidus ardor
en: Then, further, nearly two parts the burning heat

latin: adsiduusque geli casus mortalibus aufert.
en: and the unceasing fall of frost take away from mortals.

latin: quod super est arvi, tamen id natura sua vi
en: What is left of plowland, even that nature by her own force

latin: sentibus obducat, ni vis humana resistat
en: would choke with brambles, did human force not resist,

latin: vitai causa valido consueta bidenti
en: used for life's sake to groan over the strong mattock

latin: ingemere et terram pressis proscindere aratris.
en: and to cut through the earth with the plow pressed down.

latin: si non fecundas vertentes vomere glebas
en: If we did not, turning the fertile clods with the plowshare

latin: terraique solum subigentes cimus ad ortus.
en: and working the soil of the earth, rouse them to birth,

latin: sponte sua nequeant liquidas existere in auras.
en: of their own accord they could not come out into the clear air.

latin: et tamen inter dum magno quaesita labore
en: And even so, at times, when things won with great labor

latin: cum iam per terras frondent atque omnia florent,
en: are now in leaf throughout the lands and all in flower,

latin: aut nimiis torret fervoribus aetherius sol
en: either the sun in the ether scorches them with too much heat,

latin: aut subiti peremunt imbris gelidaeque pruinae
en: or sudden rains destroy them, and chill frosts,

latin: flabraque ventorum violento turbine vexant.
en: and blasts of wind harry them with violent whirlwind.

latin: praeterea genus horriferum natura ferarum
en: Further, the horror-bringing race of wild beasts,

latin: humanae genti infestum terraque marique
en: hostile to the human kind on land and sea,

latin: cur alit atque auget? cur anni tempora morbos
en: why does nature feed and increase it? Why do the seasons bring

latin: adportant? quare mors inmatura vagatur?
en: diseases? Why does untimely death go wandering?

latin: tum porro puer, ut saevis proiectus ab undis
en: Then again the child, like a sailor cast up by savage waves,

latin: navita, nudus humi iacet infans indigus omni
en: lies naked on the ground, speechless, in want of every

latin: vitali auxilio, cum primum in luminis oras
en: help for life, as soon as into the shores of light

latin: nixibus ex alvo matris natura profudit,
en: nature has poured him out with throes from his mother's womb,

latin: vagituque locum lugubri complet, ut aequumst
en: and he fills the place with mournful wailing, as is right

latin: cui tantum in vita restet transire malorum.
en: for one who has so much of evil left to pass through in life.

latin: at variae crescunt pecudes armenta feraeque
en: But the various flocks grow up, and herds, and wild beasts,

latin: nec crepitacillis opus est nec cuiquam adhibendast
en: and they need no rattles, nor must any of them be given

latin: almae nutricis blanda atque infracta loquella
en: the coaxing, broken baby-talk of a kindly nurse,

latin: nec varias quaerunt vestes pro tempore caeli,
en: nor do they look for changing clothes to suit the weather;

latin: denique non armis opus est, non moenibus altis,
en: finally, they need no arms, no high walls,

latin: qui sua tutentur, quando omnibus omnia large
en: to guard their own, since for all of them all things abundantly

latin: tellus ipsa parit naturaque daedala rerum.
en: the earth herself brings forth, and nature, artificer of things.

latin: Principio quoniam terrai corpus et umor
en: First, since the body of the earth, and moisture,

latin: aurarumque leves animae calidique vapores,
en: and the light breaths of air, and the hot vapors,

latin: e quibus haec rerum consistere summa videtur,
en: of which this sum of things is seen to consist,

latin: omnia nativo ac mortali corpore constant,
en: all consist of a body that is born and mortal,

latin: debet eodem omnis mundi natura putari.
en: the whole nature of the world must be thought to be of the same.

latin: quippe etenim, quorum partis et membra videmus
en: For indeed, things whose parts and members we see

latin: corpore nativo mortalibus esse figuris,
en: to be of a body that is born and of mortal shapes,

latin: haec eadem ferme mortalia cernimus esse
en: these same we see to be, as a rule, mortal

latin: et nativa simul. qua propter maxima mundi
en: and born as well. Therefore, since I see the greatest

latin: cum videam membra ac partis consumpta regigni,
en: members and parts of the world consumed and born again,

latin: scire licet caeli quoque item terraeque fuisse
en: we may know that heaven too, and likewise earth, have had

latin: principiale aliquod tempus clademque futuram.
en: some time of beginning, and will have their destruction.

latin: Illud in his rebus ne corripuisse rearis
en: In these matters, do not think that I have taken too much

latin: me mihi, quod terram atque ignem mortalia sumpsi
en: for granted, in assuming earth and fire to be mortal,

latin: esse neque umorem dubitavi aurasque perire
en: and in not doubting that moisture and the airs perish,

latin: atque eadem gigni rursusque augescere dixi.
en: and in saying that the same are born and grow again.

latin: principio pars terrai non nulla, perusta
en: First, no small part of the earth, scorched through

latin: solibus adsiduis, multa pulsata pedum vi,
en: by constant suns, beaten by the force of many feet,

latin: pulveris exhalat nebulam nubesque volantis,
en: breathes out a haze of dust and flying clouds,

latin: quas validi toto dispergunt aereaëre venti.
en: which strong winds scatter through all the air.

latin: pars etiam glebarum ad diluviem revocatur
en: Part of the clods too is called back to flood

latin: imbribus et ripas radentia flumina rodunt.
en: by rains, and rivers graze and gnaw their banks.

latin: praeterea pro parte sua, quod cumque alit auget,
en: Further, whatever feeds and increases another, in its share

latin: redditur; et quoniam dubio procul esse videtur
en: is given back; and since beyond doubt it is seen

latin: omniparens eadem rerum commune sepulcrum.
en: that the mother of all is also the common tomb of things,

latin: ergo terra tibi libatur et aucta recrescit.
en: therefore the earth, you see, is drawn upon and, increased, grows back.

latin: Quod super est, umore novo mare flumina fontes
en: For the rest, that the sea, the rivers, the springs always brim

latin: semper abundare et latices manare perennis
en: with new moisture, and that the waters flow without end,

latin: nil opus est verbis: magnus decursus aquarum
en: there is no need of words: the great downrush of waters

latin: undique declarat. sed primum quicquid aquai
en: declares it everywhere. But all the water that comes first

latin: tollitur in summaque fit ut nihil umor abundet,
en: is taken off, and so, in the sum, the moisture never overflows,

latin: partim quod validi verrentes aequora venti
en: partly because the strong winds sweeping the levels of the sea

latin: deminuunt radiisque retexens aetherius sol,
en: diminish it, and the sun in the ether, unweaving with rays,

latin: partim quod supter per terras diditur omnis;
en: partly because it is spread out beneath, through all the lands;

latin: percolatur enim virus retroque remanat
en: for the brine is strained out, and the matter of moisture

latin: materies umoris et ad caput amnibus omnis
en: oozes back, and all of it gathers at the heads of the rivers,

latin: convenit, inde super terras fluit agmine dulci
en: and from there flows over the lands in a column of sweet water

latin: qua via secta semel liquido pede detulit undas.
en: where the way, once cut, has carried the waves down with liquid foot.

latin: AeraAëra nunc igitur dicam, qui corpore toto
en: Now therefore I shall speak of air, which in its whole body

latin: innumerabiliter privas mutatur in horas.
en: is changed in numberless ways with every single hour.

latin: semper enim, quod cumque fluit de rebus, id omne
en: For always whatever flows off from things, all of it

latin: aerisaëris in magnum fertur mare; qui nisi contra
en: is carried into the great sea of air; and unless air in turn

latin: corpora retribuat rebus recreetque fluentis,
en: gave bodies back to things and renewed them as they flow,

latin: omnia iam resoluta forent et in aeraaëra versa.
en: all things would by now have been dissolved and turned to air.

latin: haut igitur cessat gigni de rebus et in res
en: Air therefore never ceases to be born from things and to fall

latin: reccidere, adsidue quoniam fluere omnia constat.
en: back into things, since it is certain that all things constantly flow.

latin: Largus item liquidi fons luminis, aetherius sol,
en: So too the bounteous fount of liquid light, the sun in the ether,

latin: inrigat adsidue caelum candore recenti
en: floods the sky constantly with fresh brightness

latin: suppeditatque novo confestim lumine lumen.
en: and at once supplies light with new light.

latin: nam primum quicquid fulgoris disperit ei,
en: For whatever brightness comes first is lost to it,

latin: quo cumque accidit. id licet hinc cognoscere possis,
en: wherever it falls. You may learn this from the fact

latin: quod simul ac primum nubes succedere soli
en: that as soon as clouds begin to pass beneath the sun

latin: coepere et radios inter quasi rumpere lucis,
en: and, as it were, to break apart the rays of light,

latin: extemplo inferior pars horum disperit omnis
en: at once the lower part of those rays is all lost

latin: terraque inumbratur qua nimbi cumque feruntur;
en: and the earth is shadowed wherever the storm clouds are carried;

latin: ut noscas splendore novo res semper egere
en: so that you may know things always need new brilliance,

latin: et primum iactum fulgoris quemque perire
en: and each first cast of brightness perishes,

latin: nec ratione alia res posse in sole videri,
en: and that in no other way can things be seen in the sun

latin: perpetuo ni suppeditet lucis caput ipsum.
en: unless the very fountainhead of light supplied it without end.

latin: quin etiam nocturna tibi, terrestria quae sunt,
en: Indeed, even the lights of night, the lights that are of the earth,

latin: lumina, pendentes lychni claraeque coruscis
en: hanging lamps, and torches bright with flashing

latin: fulguribus pingues multa caligine taedae
en: flares and rich with much murky smoke,

latin: consimili properant ratione, ardore ministro,
en: hurry by a like principle, with heat as their servant,

latin: suppeditare novom lumen, tremere ignibus instant,
en: to supply new light; they press on to flicker with fire,

latin: instant, nec loca lux inter quasi rupta relinquit:
en: press on, and the light leaves no place as if broken between:

latin: usque adeo properanter ab omnibus ignibus ei
en: so hurriedly is its destruction, from all its fires,

latin: exitium celeri celeratur origine flammae.
en: hastened on by the swift birth of flame.

latin: sic igitur solem lunam stellasque putandum
en: So therefore we must think that sun and moon and stars

latin: ex alio atque alio lucem iactare subortu
en: cast out their light from one fresh rising after another

latin: et primum quicquid flammarum perdere semper,
en: and always lose whatever flames come first,

latin: inviolabilia haec ne credas forte vigere.
en: so that you may not perhaps believe these thrive inviolable.

latin: Denique non lapides quoque vinci cernis ab aevo,
en: Again, do you not see that even stones are conquered by age,

latin: non altas turris ruere et putrescere saxa,
en: that high towers fall and rocks crumble,

latin: non delubra deum simulacraque fessa fatisci
en: that the gods' shrines and images grow weary and crack,

latin: nec sanctum numen fati protollere finis
en: and the holy divinity cannot push forward the bounds

latin: posse neque adversus naturae foedera niti?
en: of fate, nor struggle against nature's covenants?

latin: denique non monimenta virum dilapsa videmus,
en: Again, do we not see the monuments of men fall in ruin,

latin: quaerere proporro, sibi cumque senescere credas,
en: asking, in their turn, whether you believe that they too grow old,

latin: non ruere avolsos silices a montibus altis
en: and flints torn from the high mountains rushing down,

latin: nec validas aevi vires perferre patique
en: unable to bear and endure the strong forces of an age

latin: finiti? neque enim caderent avolsa repente,
en: that is finite? For they would not fall, torn suddenly away,

latin: ex infinito quae tempore pertolerassent
en: if from infinite time they had borne up against

latin: omnia tormenta aetatis, privata fragore.
en: all the torments of age without breaking.

latin: Denique iam tuere hoc, circum supraque quod omne
en: Again, look now at this whole, which round and above

latin: continet amplexu terram: si procreat ex se
en: holds the earth in its embrace: if it creates from itself

latin: omnia, quod quidam memorant, recipitque perempta,
en: all things, as some relate, and takes them back when they perish,

latin: totum nativum mortali corpore constat.
en: the whole consists of a body that is born and mortal.

latin: nam quod cumque alias ex se res auget alitque,
en: For whatever increases and feeds other things from itself

latin: deminui debet, recreari, cum recipit res.
en: must be diminished, and renewed when it takes things back.

latin: Praeterea si nulla fuit genitalis origo
en: Further, if there was no generative beginning

latin: terrarum et caeli semperque aeterna fuere,
en: of earth and heaven, and they have always been eternal,

latin: cur supera bellum Thebanum et funera Troiae
en: why, beyond the Theban war and the deaths of Troy,

latin: non alias alii quoque res cecinere poetaepoëtae?
en: have not other poets also sung of other things?

latin: quo tot facta virum totiens cecidere neque usquam
en: Where have so many deeds of men so often fallen, and nowhere

latin: aeternis famae monimentis insita florent?
en: flower, grafted on the eternal monuments of fame?

latin: verum, ut opinor, habet novitatem summa recensque
en: But, as I think, the whole is new, and the nature

latin: naturast mundi neque pridem exordia cepit.
en: of the world is recent, and not long ago took its beginnings.

latin: quare etiam quaedam nunc artes expoliuntur,
en: And so even now some arts are being polished,

latin: nunc etiam augescunt; nunc addita navigiis sunt
en: even now are growing; now much has been added

latin: multa, modo organici melicos peperere sonores,
en: to ships; lately players have given birth to melodious sounds;

latin: denique natura haec rerum ratioque repertast
en: finally, this nature of things and its reasoning were found

latin: nuper, et hanc primus cum primis ipse repertus
en: only lately, and I myself am now found the very first

latin: nunc ego sum in patrias qui possim vertere voces.
en: who can turn it into the speech of my fathers.

latin: Quod si forte fuisse ante hac eadem omnia credis,
en: But if perhaps you believe that all these same things were before,

latin: sed periise hominum torrenti saecla vapore,
en: but that the generations of men perished in burning heat,

latin: aut cecidisse urbis magno vexamine mundi,
en: or cities fell in some great upheaval of the world,

latin: aut ex imbribus adsiduis exisse rapaces
en: or that after constant rains ravening rivers

latin: per terras amnes atque oppida coperuisse.
en: went out across the lands and buried the towns,

latin: tanto quique magis victus fateare necessest
en: all the more must you, conquered, confess

latin: exitium quoque terrarum caelique futurum;
en: that destruction of earth and heaven too will come;

latin: nam cum res tantis morbis tantisque periclis
en: for when things were assailed by such diseases and such

latin: temptarentur, ibi si tristior incubuisset
en: dangers, then, if a grimmer cause had pressed upon them,

latin: causa, darent late cladem magnasque ruinas.
en: they would have spread disaster and great ruin far and wide.

latin: nec ratione alia mortales esse videmur,
en: Nor in any other way do we seem to be mortal,

latin: inter nos nisi quod morbis aegrescimus isdem
en: among ourselves, save that we sicken with the same diseases

latin: atque illi quos a vita natura removit.
en: as those whom nature has removed from life.

latin: Praeterea quae cumque manent aeterna necessust
en: Further, whatever things endure eternal must, of necessity,

latin: aut, quia sunt solido cum corpore, respuere ictus
en: either, because they are of solid body, repel blows

latin: nec penetrare pati sibi quicquam quod queat artas
en: and suffer nothing to enter them that could tear apart

latin: dissociare intus partis, ut materiai
en: their close-knit parts within, as the bodies of matter

latin: corpora sunt, quorum naturam ostendimus ante,
en: are, whose nature we have shown before;

latin: aut ideo durare aetatem posse per omnem,
en: or be able to last through all time for this reason,

latin: plagarum quia sunt expertia, sicut inane est,
en: that they are exempt from blows, as the void is,

latin: quod manet intactum neque ab ictu fungitur hilum,
en: which stays untouched and is not affected one whit by a stroke;

latin: aut etiam quia nulla loci sit copia circum,
en: or else because there is no supply of place around them

latin: quo quasi res possint discedere dissoluique,
en: into which things could, as it were, part and be dissolved,

latin: sicut summarum summa est aeterna, neque extra
en: as the sum of sums is eternal, nor is there outside it

latin: qui locus est quo dissiliant neque corpora sunt quae
en: any place into which they might scatter, nor are there bodies that

latin: possint incidere et valida dissolvere plaga.
en: could fall upon them and dissolve them with a strong blow.

latin: at neque, uti docui, solido cum corpore mundi
en: But neither, as I have taught, is the nature of the world

latin: naturast, quoniam admixtumst in rebus inane,
en: of solid body, since void is mixed in things,

latin: nec tamen est ut inane, neque autem corpora desunt,
en: nor yet is it like the void; nor indeed are bodies lacking

latin: ex infinito quae possint forte coorta
en: that might perhaps gather together out of the infinite

latin: corruere hanc rerum violento turbine summam
en: and overthrow this sum of things with a violent whirlwind

latin: aut aliam quamvis cladem inportare pericli,
en: or bring upon it some other disaster of danger,

latin: nec porro natura loci spatiumque profundi
en: nor further is the nature of place and the space of the deep

latin: deficit, exspargi quo possint moenia mundi,
en: lacking, into which the walls of the world could be scattered,

latin: aut alia quavis possunt vi pulsa perire.
en: or, driven by any other force, perish.

latin: haut igitur leti praeclusa est ianua caelo
en: The door of death, therefore, is not shut to the sky,

latin: nec soli terraeque neque altis aequoris undis,
en: nor to sun and earth, nor to the deep waters of the sea,

latin: sed patet immani et vasto respectat hiatu.
en: but stands open and looks toward them with its vast and monstrous gape.

latin: quare etiam nativa necessumst confiteare
en: Therefore you must confess that these same things

latin: haec eadem; neque enim, mortali corpore quae sunt,
en: were born; for things that are of mortal body

latin: ex infinito iam tempore adhuc potuissent
en: could not, from infinite time until now,

latin: inmensi validas aevi contemnere vires.
en: have scorned the strong forces of immeasurable age.

latin: Denique tantopere inter se cum maxima mundi
en: Finally, since the greatest members of the world

latin: pugnent membra, pio nequaquam concita bello,
en: fight so among themselves, stirred by a war in no way holy,

latin: nonne vides aliquam longi certaminis ollis
en: do you not see that some end of their long contest

latin: posse dari finem, vel cum sol et vapor omnis
en: can be granted them, as when the sun and all heat

latin: omnibus epotis umoribus exsuperarint?
en: have drunk up all the moisture and prevailed?

latin: quod facere intendunt, neque adhuc conata patrantur;
en: This they strive to do, and have not yet carried out their attempt;

latin: tantum suppeditant amnes ultraque minantur
en: so much do the rivers supply, and they threaten besides

latin: omnia diluviare ex alto gurgite ponti:
en: to flood all things from the deep gulf of the sea:

latin: ne quiquam, quoniam verrentes aequora venti
en: in vain, since the winds that sweep the levels of the sea

latin: deminuunt radiisque retexens aetherius sol,
en: diminish it, and the sun in the ether, unweaving with rays,

latin: et siccare prius confidunt omnia posse
en: and they trust that they can dry all things up

latin: quam liquor incepti possit contingere finem.
en: before the water can reach the end of its undertaking.

latin: tantum spirantes aequo certamine bellum
en: Breathing such war in an equal contest,

latin: magnis inter se de rebus cernere certant,
en: they strive to settle great matters between them,

latin: cum semel interea fuerit superantior ignis
en: though once, meanwhile, fire has been the stronger,

latin: et semel, ut fama est, umor regnarit in arvis.
en: and once, as the story goes, water reigned over the fields.

latin: ignis enim superavit et ambiens multa perussit,
en: For fire prevailed and, ranging around, burned up much,

latin: avia cum Phaethonta rapax vis solis equorum
en: when the ravening force of the sun's horses swept Phaethon

latin: aethere raptavit toto terrasque per omnis.
en: off the road through the whole ether and over all the lands.

latin: at pater omnipotens ira tum percitus acri
en: But the father almighty, roused then with bitter anger,

latin: magnanimum Phaethonta repenti fulminis ictu
en: with a sudden stroke of the thunderbolt dashed great-hearted

latin: deturbavit equis in terram, Solque cadenti
en: Phaethon from the horses to the earth, and the Sun, meeting him

latin: obvius aeternam succepit lampada mundi
en: as he fell, caught up the eternal lamp of the world,

latin: disiectosque redegit equos iunxitque trementis,
en: and brought back the scattered horses and yoked them, trembling,

latin: inde suum per iter recreavit cuncta gubernans,
en: then, steering them on their own road, restored all things,

latin: scilicet ut veteres Graium cecinere poetaepoëtae.
en: as, to be sure, the old poets of the Greeks have sung.

latin: quod procul a vera nimis est ratione repulsum.
en: But this is driven very far away from true reasoning.

latin: ignis enim superare potest ubi materiai
en: For fire can prevail when more bodies of matter

latin: ex infinito sunt corpora plura coorta;
en: have risen up out of the infinite;

latin: inde cadunt vires aliqua ratione revictae,
en: then its forces fall, overcome by some principle,

latin: aut pereunt res exustae torrentibus auris.
en: or else things perish, burned up by the scorching air.

latin: umor item quondam coepit superare coortus,
en: Water likewise once rose up and began to prevail,

latin: ut fama est, hominum vitas quando obruit undis;
en: as report says, when it drowned the lives of men in its waves;

latin: inde ubi vis aliqua ratione aversa recessit,
en: then, when that force was turned aside by some principle and withdrew,

latin: ex infinito fuerat quae cumque coorta,
en: whatever of it had risen up out of the infinite,

latin: constiterunt imbres et flumina vim minuerunt.
en: the rains stopped and the rivers lessened their force.

latin: Sed quibus ille modis coniectus materiai
en: But by what means that gathering of matter

latin: fundarit terram et caelum pontique profunda,
en: founded the earth and the sky and the depths of the sea,

latin: solis lunai cursus, ex ordine ponam.
en: the courses of the sun and the moon, I shall set out in order.

latin: nam certe neque consilio primordia rerum
en: For certainly the first-beginnings of things did not by design

latin: ordine se suo quaeque sagaci mente locarunt
en: set themselves each in its order with a shrewd mind,

latin: nec quos quaeque darent motus pepigere profecto;
en: nor, surely, did they bargain what motions each should give;

latin: sed quia multa modis multis primordia rerum
en: but because many first-beginnings of things in many ways,

latin: ex infinito iam tempore percita plagis
en: driven by blows from infinite time till now,

latin: ponderibusque suis consuerunt concita ferri
en: and roused by their own weights, have been used to move

latin: omnimodisque coire atque omnia pertemptare,
en: and to meet in every way and to try out all things

latin: quae cumque inter se possent congressa creare,
en: that they could create by meeting with one another,

latin: propterea fit uti magnum volgata per aevom
en: therefore it comes about that, spread abroad through a great age,

latin: omnigenus coetus et motus experiundo
en: by trying every kind of union and motion

latin: tandem conveniant ea quae coniecta repente
en: at last those come together which, suddenly thrown together,

latin: magnarum rerum fiunt exordia saepe,
en: often become the origins of great things,

latin: terrai maris et caeli generisque animantum.
en: of earth and sea and sky and the race of living things.

latin: Hic neque tum solis rota cerni lumine largo
en: At that time neither could the sun's wheel be seen with its ample light

latin: altivolans poterat nec magni sidera mundi
en: flying on high, nor the stars of the great world,

latin: nec mare nec caelum nec denique terra neque aeraër
en: nor sea nor sky nor, finally, earth nor air,

latin: nec similis nostris rebus res ulla videri,
en: nor could anything be seen like the things we know,

latin: sed nova tempestas quaedam molesque coorta.
en: but a kind of strange storm and a mass, risen up.

latin: diffugere inde loci partes coepere paresque
en: Then parts began to fly apart from one another, and like things

latin: cum paribus iungi res et discludere mundum
en: to join with like, and to mark off the world,

latin: membraque dividere et magnas disponere partes
en: and to divide its members and arrange its great parts

latin: omnigenis e principiis, discordia quorum
en: out of beginnings of every kind, whose discord confounded

latin: intervalla vias conexus pondera plagas
en: intervals, paths, connections, weights, blows,

latin: concursus motus turbabat proelia miscens
en: collisions, motions, stirring up battles among them

latin: propter dissimilis formas variasque figuras,
en: because of their unlike forms and varied shapes,

latin: quod non omnia sic poterant coniuncta manere
en: since not all, joined thus, could stay together

latin: nec motus inter sese dare convenientis,
en: nor give one another fitting motions:

latin: hoc est, a terris altum secernere caelum,
en: that is, to separate the high sky from the earth,

latin: et sorsum mare, uti secreto umore pateret,
en: and the sea apart, to spread with its moisture set apart,

latin: seorsus item puri secretique aetheris ignes.
en: and apart too the fires of the pure and separate ether.

latin: Quippe etenim primum terrai corpora quaeque,
en: For indeed, first, all the bodies of earth,

latin: propterea quod erant gravia et perplexa, coibant
en: because they were heavy and entangled, came together

latin: in medio atque imas capiebant omnia sedes;
en: in the middle and all took the lowest seats;

latin: quae quanto magis inter se perplexa coibant,
en: and the more, entangled, they came together among themselves,

latin: tam magis expressere ea quae mare sidera solem
en: the more they squeezed out those which would make the sea, the stars, the sun

latin: lunamque efficerent et magni moenia mundi;
en: and the moon and the walls of the great world;

latin: omnia enim magis haec e levibus atque rutundis
en: for all these are made more of smooth and round

latin: seminibus multoque minoribus sunt elementis
en: seeds and of much smaller elements

latin: quam tellus. ideo per rara foramina terrae
en: than the earth is. And so through the open pores of the earth,

latin: partibus erumpens primus se sustulit aether
en: breaking out in parts, the ether first lifted itself up,

latin: ignifer et multos secum levis abstulit ignis,

latin: eiectique domo fugiebant saxea tecta

en: They in their ignorance often poured out poison

latin: tum genus humanum primum mollescere coepit.

latin: et pueros commendarunt muliebreque saeclum,

latin: vocibus et gestu cum balbe significarent

latin: nec tamen omnimodis poterat concordia gigni,

latin: sed bona magnaque pars servabat foedera caste;

latin: cornua nata prius vitulo quam frontibus extent,

latin: illis iratus petit atque infestus inurget.

en: And day by day they showed more and more how to exchange

latin: condere coeperunt urbis arcemque locare
en: Kings began to found cities and to set up a citadel

en: and they divided flocks and fields and gave them out

latin: posterius res inventast aurumque repertum,
en: Later, property was invented and gold discovered,

latin: quod facile et validis et pulchris dempsit honorem;
en: which easily robbed the strong and the beautiful of their honor;

latin: divitioris enim sectam plerumque secuntur

latin: quod siquis vera vitam ratione gubernet,
en: But if one were to steer his life by true reasoning,

latin: divitiae grandes homini sunt vivere parce

latin: at claros homines voluerunt se atque potentes,
en: But men wanted themselves famous and powerful,

latin: ut fundamento stabili fortuna maneret
en: so that their fortune might rest on a firm foundation

latin: et placidam possent opulenti degere vitam,
en: and they, being wealthy, might pass a calm life:

latin: ne quiquam, quoniam ad summum succedere honorem
en: in vain, since, struggling to climb to the highest honor,

latin: certantes iter infestum fecere viai,
en: they made the road they traveled full of danger,

latin: et tamen e summo, quasi fulmen, deicit ictos
en: and yet from the summit, like a thunderbolt, it hurls them, struck,

latin: invidia inter dum contemptim in Tartara taetra;
en: envy does, at times, contemptuously, into foul Tartarus;

latin: invidia quoniam ceu fulmine summa vaporant
en: since by envy, as by the thunderbolt, the summits are scorched

latin: plerumque et quae sunt aliis magis edita cumque;
en: as a rule, and whatever stands raised above the rest;

latin: ut satius multo iam sit parere quietum
en: so that it is far better now to obey in quiet

latin: quam regere imperio res velle et regna tenere.
en: than to want to rule the world by command and hold kingdoms.

latin: proinde sine in cassum defessi sanguine sudent,
en: So let them sweat blood, worn out, to no purpose,

latin: angustum per iter luctantes ambitionis;
en: struggling along the narrow road of ambition;

latin: quandoquidem sapiunt alieno ex ore petuntque
en: since they are wise from another's mouth, and seek

latin: res ex auditis potius quam sensibus ipsis,
en: things from what they hear rather than from their own senses,

latin: nec magis id nunc est neque erit mox quam fuit ante.
en: and this is no more so now, nor will be soon, than it was before.

latin: Ergo regibus occisis subversa iacebat
en: Therefore, the kings slain, there lay overthrown

latin: pristina maiestas soliorum et sceptra superba,
en: the ancient majesty of thrones and the proud scepters,

latin: et capitis summi praeclarum insigne cruentum
en: and the glorious emblem of the highest head, bloodied,

latin: sub pedibus vulgi magnum lugebat honorem;
en: beneath the feet of the mob mourned its great honor;

latin: nam cupide conculcatur nimis ante metutum.
en: for what was too much feared before is eagerly trampled.

latin: res itaque ad summam faecem turbasque redibat,
en: And so things went back to the lowest dregs and turmoil,

latin: imperium sibi cum ac summatum quisque petebat.

latin: inde magistratum partim docuere creare
en: Then some of them taught men to create magistrates

latin: iuraque constituere, ut vellent legibus uti.
en: and to establish rights, so that they would consent to use laws.

latin: nam genus humanum, defessum vi colere aevom,
en: For the human race, worn out with living its life by force,

latin: ex inimicitiis languebat; quo magis ipsum
en: was languishing from its feuds; all the more readily
